name: generosity

attributes.attribute: half-Fomorian king whose stinginess led to dethronement
driven from his throne by satires and died miserably
believed to punish the ungenerous in post-Celtic times
translated into a general demand for hospitality

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: In Celtic belief generosity formed a key value. An ancient royal generosity became a general demand for hospitality. This hospitality applied especially to strangers. Failing this value brought punishment. The half-Fomorian king Bres proved ungenerous. Satires drove him from his throne. He died miserably for his greed and stinginess. In post-Celtic times the fairies kept this value alive. People feared that the fairies would punish the ungenerous. This fear preserved the priority given to hospitality. Generosity stood among the sacred requirements of a Celtic king, beside the geis.

okr.objective: Describe generosity and hospitality as a central Celtic value.
